Applied.Outcome: All ten decisions taken as recommended and written in under "Decided before the build".

Replies.Text:
Design for Step 3. Each point is a decision with my recommendation; resolve with no reply to take them all, or answer the ones you want otherwise.

1. Getting CodeMirror 6 into the page with no build step. CodeMirror 6 is a dozen small ES-module packages with bare imports between them (@codemirror/state, view, language, commands, search, lang-markdown; @lezer/common, highlight, markdown, lr; style-mod, w3c-keyname, crelt, @marijn/find-cluster-break). I recommend: npm install them as dependencies (pinned, like monaco-editor), serve each package's dist folder at /vendor/codemirror/<package>/ from where require resolves it (attach_vendor in Server.js, which the desktop's page server shares), an import map in index.html naming the bare specifiers, and one module script of ours, public/js/codemirror-bundle.js, that imports what the page uses and puts it on window.CodeMirror6 for the plain scripts. Chrome and Electron read import maps; nothing is bundled or copied.

2. One Edit view, two engines. Rather than a second component that repeats monaco-edit's 180 lines of drafts, stale checks, Save and the preview, monaco-edit becomes edit-view: the same template and controller, with the editor behind one small interface, Create( Element, Text, OnChange ), Get, Set, Focus, Layout, Dispose, and for the comment boxes Plain( Element, Text, OnChange, OnSubmit ) returning { Get, Set, Focus, Dispose, LineHeight }. Two factories give it: Editor (Monaco, as it is, wrapped) and Mirror (CodeMirror). The setting picks the factory when the view opens; a change of setting takes effect at the next open. That is still "the CodeMirror editor beside Monaco, chosen by a setting", with one place for the editing logic. The alternative is a codemirror-edit twin and a shared Editing service; say so if you prefer the two tags.

3. The setting. "In Settings" would put it in the owner's consensus.json popup, which is the server's; the choice is the browser's, like the theme and the size. I recommend an Editor select beside Theme and Scale at the bottom of the sidebar (Monaco, CodeMirror), remembered under consensus.editor, default Monaco for now. The preview's hidden flag is remembered per engine: Monaco keeps preview-hidden as it is; CodeMirror has its own, starting hidden, and the Preview button shows it.

4. The anchor map. The server finds each thread in the rendered plain text (Anchors.PlainText: marked's HTML with the tags gone, block tags as breaks, entities decoded, whitespace collapsed, trimmed). On the client, from the Lezer markdown tree of the source: walk the tree, keep the text of the content nodes and skip the syntax (heading, emphasis, code and link marks, URLs, list and quote marks, HTML tags, image syntax), decode entities and backslash escapes, collapse whitespace the same way, and keep for every kept character its source offset. Then check the result against the plain text the client can compute the server's way (marked is in the page; PlainText's few regexes port as they are). Equal: each thread's Found Start and End map to source offsets. Not equal: no highlights in the editor for that text (the threads stay listed), and a console line names the first differing position, so the gap can be closed. The map is an ES module of its own, public/js/anchormap.js, used by the bundle and imported by a node test that runs it over a corpus (the docs guide's pages, the Consensus project's texts) against src/Anchors.js's own PlainText. That is the first page-side logic with a node test, and the place where the cases will be found.

5. Highlights in the editor: a StateField of mark decorations (class anchor, the state, selected, several, data-threads as the html-view's marks carry), set by an effect when the plan loads, the selection changes or Highlight changes, and mapped through the document's changes as you type, so the marks follow the text until Save, when the server finds the anchors again and the field is reset. A mousedown on a mark selects its thread (the next one on a passage of several, as the html-view does) and scrolls its card into view. No selection buttons in the editor in this step.

6. What the CodeMirror editor has: line numbers, the fold gutter (headings fold), line wrapping, history, the default and search keymaps (find and replace, Ctrl+F), indent with Tab, multiple selections, the active line, markdown highlighting from the default style; Ctrl+S saves through a keymap, Ctrl+E reaches it through the page's hotkeys, whose in_editor learns .cm-editor beside .monaco-editor. The theme is built from the page's palette variables (background, text, muted, panel, accent) in a Compartment reconfigured on consensus-theme, dark or light as the page is.

7. The comment boxes follow the setting: comment-editor asks the chosen factory for Plain; the CodeMirror box has wrapping, no gutters, Ctrl+Enter in its keymap, the same height and grip. The two Plain boxes share the { Get, Set, Focus, Dispose, LineHeight } shape, so the component does not know which it holds.

8. Styles: codemirror's own .cm-editor rules are in the theme (JavaScript); the editor box in edit-view.css takes both engines; the anchor classes inside .cm-content reuse html-view's colours (the same variables) in edit-view.css.

9. Checkpoints: (1) the vendor route, the import map, the bundle module, the Mirror factory with Create and Plain, and the anchor map with its node test; (2) edit-view with the engine interface, the Editor factory wrapped to it, the setting in the sidebar, the per-engine preview flag; (3) the highlights and the click in the editor, comment-editor on the chosen engine, the hotkeys and the theme; (4) the browser tests and the screenshots.

10. The smoke: the anchor map's node test over the corpus; the browser tests gain one: the setting switched to CodeMirror, Edit opens a .cm-editor whose marks count the threads with a position, a mark's click selects the thread, typing before a mark keeps it on its words, Ctrl+S saves and the marks are found again, the preview is hidden by default and shows on the button, the reply box is a CodeMirror box and Ctrl+Enter posts; Monaco's tests unchanged with the setting at Monaco. Screenshots of the CodeMirror Edit view with the marks, light and dark.

Applied.Outcome: The build was accepted as reported; no text change. Committed as "UI Components: Step 3".

Replies.Text:
Build log, Step 3: CodeMirror Editor. Built by Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1) through the Claude Code CLI, as the ten decisions say. Not committed yet: resolve to accept, and I commit it as "UI Components: Step 3".

What was built, and where:
- The packages: @codemirror/state, view, language, commands, search and lang-markdown as pinned dependencies (package.json), 23 packages with everything under them. Server.js's attach_vendor serves each at /vendor/codemirror/<name>/ from where require resolves it (CodeMirrorPackages, exported for the test); index.html carries the import map and loads public/js/codemirror-bundle.js, a module of ours that puts the pieces on window.CodeMirror6 and says codemirror-ready.
- public/js/anchormap.js, an ES module: Build( source ) gives the plain text with a source span per character from the Lezer tree (CommonMark with GFM, as marked's default), PlainTextOfHtml is the server's rule, SourceRange maps a plain range to the source. test/AnchorMap.test.js runs it over the guide's pages, the fifty texts of the Consensus project in .consensus and three made-up cases: every plain text equals the server's PlainText character for character, every span holds its character, a range maps, and index.html's import map names exactly the packages the server serves.
- public/js/mirror.js, the Mirror factory: Create with line numbers, the fold gutter, wrapping, history, the default and search keymaps, Tab indent, multiple selections, the active line and markdown highlighting; Plain for the comment boxes with Ctrl+Enter; a theme from the palette variables in a Compartment, rebuilt on consensus-theme; the anchors as a StateField of marks set by an effect and mapped through the document's changes, a second effect restyling for the selected thread, and a mousedown on a mark handing the threads under it to the view.
- public/js/editor.js, Monaco behind the same interface: one instance per Create, Ctrl+S and Ctrl+Enter handled on the instance (addCommand's bindings are Monaco-wide and pile up), Dispose freeing it and emptying the element.
- monaco-edit is edit-view (public/components/edit-view): the same template and controller with the editor behind the interface, the engine picked from State.Editor when the view opens, the other one disposed; in a CodeMirror editor the anchors are set on the saved text (the server's positions through the anchor map, filtered as Highlight says), follow the text through edits, and are set afresh after a save; a mark's click selects its thread (the next of several) and scrolls its card. Threads.Highlighted now holds the Highlight rule for html-view and edit-view both.
- The setting: an Editor select beside Theme and Scale at the bottom of the sidebar (State.Editor, consensus.editor, default Monaco); the preview's hidden flag per engine (preview-hidden, preview-hidden-codemirror starting hidden); comment-editor takes the chosen engine's Plain; hotkeys.js's in_editor knows .cm-editor.
- Styles: edit-view.css gives CodeMirror its height and scrolling and the anchor classes inside .cm-content in html-view's colours; the sidebar's three controls wrap, so the editor's sits on a second row.

Decided during the build:
1. The anchor map needed four rules beyond the first draft to match the server over the corpus: table cells read as breaks (the pipes between them render as <td>s), a bare URL is text while a link's target is not, a hard break is a space (the server treats br as a block tag), and a bracketed phrase is a link only when its label is defined, since Lezer parses every [text] as a reference link and marked does not. The test will show any case the corpus does not hold.
2. CodeMirror's default highlight style is made for a light page (dark navy marks and URLs vanished on the dark palette), so the Mirror theme carries a highlight style of its own from the palette: headings and strong bold, emphasis italic, links in the accent, the syntax marks, URLs, list and quote marks muted.
3. A plain box's line height is read from the theme's computed styles, which apply at once; CodeMirror's own measure comes a frame later, and a frame's wait for it let the compose box lose its focus in three browser tests.
4. A mark that wraps onto two lines has its bounding box's centre between them, where no text is; the browser test clicks the mark's first line box. A person's click lands on text.
5. The highlights in the editor are set when the editor's text is the saved text. A draft opened from a tab keeps the marks it had, following the text; Highlight's picker applies to a dirty editor at its next save.
6. The edit-view's section carries an engine-<name> class, for styles that may want to tell them apart later; none do yet.

How it was tested:
- npm test: 186 tests. The whole suite passed once with every test green and once with one failure in Api.test.js's run test (a 409 expected for a second run while the first runs; under the parallel load the stand-in command had already finished, so the server answered 201); Api.test.js alone passes, and nothing of the runs changed in this step. The browser tests gained one for the CodeMirror path: the setting switched through the sidebar's select, Edit opens a .cm-editor and no Monaco, the preview starts hidden and shows on the button, the two threads' passages are marked by state, a mark's click selects the thread in the pane and in the text, typing at the top keeps the marks on their words, Ctrl+S saves revision 3 and the marks are found again, the reply box is a CodeMirror box and Ctrl+Enter posts, and the setting back to Monaco opens Monaco. The 28 earlier tests run with Monaco as before.
- Over temporary servers: the bundle loads with no console errors; the Edit view and the reply box in both engines; the highlights, the click, the edit, the save, an apply by the LLM; the dark palette. Screenshots of the CodeMirror Edit view with the marks, light and dark.
- Your running desktop was restarted on your word after checkpoint 1, so your page serves the vendor route; a reload shows the Editor select at the bottom of the sidebar.

Not in this step: the selection buttons in the editor and Live Preview (the later plan); the guide (Step 6).
